The Best Beef Enchiladas of My Life—In Hanoi!
Mar 2026 • Couples
If you’re looking for authentic Mexican flavors in Hanoi, Salt n' Lime is an absolute must-visit. From the moment the first round of chips and salsa arrived alongside our margaritas, we knew we were in for a treat.
As someone who was raised in Southern California and used to cross the border on weekends specifically for authentic Mexican food, I have very high standards. Salt n' Lime didn't just meet them—they blew them away.
The Highlights:
The Margaritas & Starters: The margaritas are expertly mixed, and the chips and salsa are the perfect opening act.
The Burritos: Massive, fresh, and flavorful.
The Beef Enchiladas: These were beyond belief. I can honestly say they are hands down the best I have ever eaten. The depth of flavor is something you usually only find in a family kitchen in Mexico.
The Service:
The manager is awesome and clearly brings a wealth of high-level restaurant experience to the floor. The service is seamless, and you can tell the entire team cares about the quality of your experience.
Bottom line: Whether you're a local or just passing through Vietnam, go to Salt n' Lime. You will not be disappointed!

One of the more average Tay Ho Mexican offerings
Jun 2024 • Friends
Came here as it was close to a bar. I was going with friends afterwards. I have eaten here before a while ago, and if I'm honest, it didn't really stand out as amazing then either.
The burritos are very nice, although there are bo sauce condinents on the table to add more flavour or spice if desired. We ordered chips and guacamole, and they are stingy on the portion size of guac. Even though we ordered a bowl, it isn't enough to cover half the chips they provide.
Margarita is very average, although other drinks were good.
Service is friendly, but there really is so much choice for Mexican food around and this is not on the same level at those.

Confused
Jul 2020
To start, I'm from Kansas and lived in Texas. So I’m familiar with BBQ and Tex-Mex. when you enter the premises there’s a huge smoker, ideal for BBQed meats. And this is my dilemma. Why use BBQ pork shoulder for Mexican dishes. Why not make carnitas pork, or al pastor and be more authentic. My brain got confused. I kept wanting BBQ sauce and coleslaw. I think the owner needs to go full bore BBQ food and call it good. The pulled pork was excellent....but not in my burrito. 

 Staff was nebulous but adequate...sometimes. Margaritas the best.
